subject: gk
question:
Which of the following pair of compound–general formulas is correct?

I. Alkenes – CₙH₂ₙ

II. Alkanes – CₙH₂ₙ−₁
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A common family of hydrocarbons found in crude oil is alkenes.
 
• In this family, there is **at least one carbon–carbon double bond.**
 
• This double bond makes a big difference to the chemistry of the compounds of the family.
 
• The alkenes like all hydrocarbons, burn in the air to form carbon dioxide and water.
 
• In oxygen, ethene reacts strongly so it isn't much good as energy.
 
• The alkenes are also too useful in the chemical assiduity for the manufacture of plastics and numerous other chemicals to be used as energy.
 
• Alkanes have the formula **CₙH₂ₙ₊₂**. Therefore 2nd statement is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The** alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain one triple bond,** the general formula of alkynes is CnH₂ₙ₋₂ and the triple bond is known as the ‘acetylenic bond’.
 
• Many alkynes have been found in nature**. Ethyne (C₂H₂) is the first member of the alkyne family, with two carbon atoms connected by a triple bond.**
